Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call follow-up (latency, throughput, sizing)

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our performance/SLO discussion so we have a clear plan for the dedicated capacity validation: 

Summary of requirements you shared
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for streaming responses (targeting <150ms if possible); p50 ideally <100ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: steady-state 100 QPS with peaks to 250 QPS; typical concurrency ~40 sessions, occasional spikes to 120.
- Streaming: client expects chunked token streaming (low initial latency per chunk, ~50–100ms between chunks).
- Payload size: average prompt ~120 tokens, average generation ~60 tokens (you confirmed distribution skewed to short completions).

What Redwood will validate
1) GPU type comparisons: we’ll run the same model workload across H100-80GB reserved nodes, A100-40GB nodes, and L4-class cost-optimized nodes to show tradeoffs (latency/throughput/cost).
2) Reserved throughput sizing: we’ll estimate reserved vCPU/GPU capacity required to meet 95th/50th SLO targets under your observed token distribution.
3) Concurrency & batching behavior: measure latency degradation as concurrency increases and tune batching/autoscale parameters.
4) Streaming behavior: verify chunk latency and number-of-chunk tradeoffs with KV cache warm-up.

Attachments: I’ve attached our initial benchmark summary (gpu_benchmark_summary.pdf) and the raw CSV from last week’s baseline (latency_test_results_v1.csv). Also linking a short test plan in Drive.

Proposed validation plan (high level)
- You confirm the model variant you intend to serve (e.g., Llama2-13B, MPT-30B) and whether you require quantized variants.
- Redwood provisions a 2–4 hour dedicated test window in our staging cluster (isolated) and runs three test legs: H100 baseline, A100 comparison, L4 cost test.
- Each leg: 30m warm-up (cache fills), 60m steady-state load simulating your distribution (100 QPS baseline, 250 QPS burst), 30m ramp-down.
- Deliverables: latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), per-GPU throughput, cost estimate for reserved capacity to hit SLOs, tuning recommendations (batch size, autoscale triggers).

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm model name + size and whether streaming is mandatory for all endpoints.
2) Confirm a staging endpoint or allow Redwood to use a Redwood-managed test setup with synthetic traffic.
3) Any special tokens/firmware/LLM prompt examples you want included in the test set.

If that plan looks good I’ll loop in Marissa and Aditya to schedule the tests (and copy Rachel for success/enablement and Rishi for commercial sizing). Can we aim for Friday 20 Feb for the test window?

Thanks —
Rafael

--

Thanks Rafael — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Model: we’ll likely serve an Llama2-13B fine-tuned variant (float16). We may also try an INT8-quantized variant for cost comparison but streaming must work for the primary float16 endpoint.
- Token distribution: after sampling our logs, median prompt ~110 tokens, mean ~130; median generation ~45 tokens, mean ~60. We do ~70% short completions (<64 tokens) and 30% medium (64–256).
- Concurrency: typical concurrent users in a peak shard is ~35–45; global peaks hit 110–130 concurrent sessions. We care most about the 95th percentile user latency for interactive flows.
- Staging access: we can stand up a staging ingress and provide API keys for your tests. I’ll work with Tom to create the keys and share a staging URL.

Two asks for Redwood: please include a rough cost delta between H100 and A100 for the reserved throughput you recommend, and call out any model-size limitations for L4-type nodes.

I’m OK with Friday 20 Feb — Tom and I are available morning PT.

Best,
Sophie

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call follow-up (latency, throughput, sizing)

Thanks — adding a few technical notes and what we’ll measure during the Friday run so expectations are clear.

Quick GPU throughput ballpark (single-streaming session / mixed short sequences) using Llama2-13B float16 baseline:
- H100-80GB (opt-level kernels, KV cache warm): ~350–480 RPS equivalent for short+streaming workloads (depends on chunking). Strongest for low p95 latency.
- A100-40GB: ~220–320 RPS equivalent; higher p95 vs H100 for heavy streaming but much cheaper by hour.
- L4-class (4–8GB): ~60–140 RPS; best for cost-optimized inference on shorter sequences and stateless calls, but not ideal if you need large KV cache for long context.

Notes:
- Streaming penalty: chunked streaming increases p95 slightly vs purely batched non-streaming. We’ll measure chunk time (time-to-first-chunk and inter-chunk latency).
- Batching: we’ll run with conservative auto-batching (max batch size tuned per-GPU). For interactive SLOs we bias latency over throughput (small batch size, aggressive autoscale).
- Reserved throughput sizing: given your distribution (mean 130 tokens in, mean 60 out) and target 95th latency <=200ms, our preliminary estimate is:
  * H100: 2–3 GPUs reserved to cover baseline 100 QPS with safe headroom for bursts to 250 QPS (autoscale for bursts).
  * A100: 3–5 GPUs reserved to hit equivalent p95 (depends on batching and cache hit).
  * L4: not recommended as primary for this SLO; good as a supplement for low-cost, low-latency infrequent routes.

Suggested Friday test variables:
- Model: Llama2-13B float16 (primary), Llama2-13B int8 (secondary)
- Sequence dist: 70% short (<64 gen), 30% medium (64–256 gen)
- Concurrency patterns: steady 100 QPS, 3x 2-minute bursts to 250 QPS
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, per-device GPU util, memory pressure, per-request cost estimate

I’ve attached a short test plan (dedicated-capacity-test-plan.md) and the recent CSV from our quick bench run. If Sophie can share the staging keys and any sample prompts we’ll plug them in.

I’ll be on the call Friday morning PT to run the tests and interpret results in real time.

—
Marissa Cole
